headline: FED WALLER SIGNALS RATE HOLD — GOLD SURGES $90 FROM NFP LOWS; HIKE ODDS HALVED TO 50%
snippet: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would support holding rates steady at the September 15–16 FOMC meeting if August inflation data continues to improve, sending gold surging roughly $90 from Friday's NFP-driven low of $4,374 to $4,465+. Markets cut rate-hike odds from 70% to approximately 50%. Waller's conditional language — 'If inflation comes in hot, I would consider a hike' — keeps August CPI (due September 12) as the single most important print for metals before the FOMC. Waller noted three-month core inflation has fallen from 4.76% in February to 3.05% — 'better than headline numbers suggest.'

headline: DUTCH CENTRAL BANK PULLS 86 TONNES OF GOLD FROM NORTH AMERICA — GEOPOLITICAL REPATRIATION WAVE BUILDS
snippet: De Nederlandsche Bank transferred 86 tonnes of gold — worth over €10 billion — from North America to London between March and August 2026, citing 'increasing geopolitical unrest' and a desire to 'strengthen crisis preparedness.' DNB sold 59 tonnes in New York and purchased equivalent gold in London, while physically moving 27+ tonnes from U.S. and Canadian vaults. North America's share of Dutch gold reserves fell from 51% to 37%; London's rose from 18% to 32%. Experts link the move to friction with the Trump administration. Austria, Italy, and Turkey are signalling similar repatriation intentions.

headline: PALADIN PLS URANIUM: 42M INCL. 12.5M AT 1.8% U3O8 — ATLAS DISCOVERY KEEPS EXPANDING; TSX: PDN
snippet: Paladin Energy's Patterson Lake South project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin delivered another batch of strong drill results from the Atlas discovery, first announced in June. Standout hole PLS26-782 returned 42.1 metres of total composite mineralisation, including 12.5 metres grading 1.8% eU₃O₈. Seventeen new holes since June 25 have confirmed Atlas is growing in multiple directions, 3.5km south of the flagship Triple R deposit. The expanded footprint sets up a potentially significant resource upgrade ahead.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS SLASHES GOLD TARGET TO $4,900 FROM $5,400 — RATE CUTS NOW MARCH 2027
snippet: Goldman Sachs Research cut its year-end 2026 gold price forecast to $4,900/oz from $5,400, citing a delayed Federal Reserve rate-cut timeline — the bank now expects the first cut in March 2027, not late 2026. Despite the downgrade, Goldman's analysts say the structural bull case — central banks steadily reallocating reserves away from foreign currencies — remains intact. Tactically cautious, structurally constructive: Goldman sees near-term downside risk from the elevated rate environment but medium-term upside as easing eventually arrives.

headline: ZIJIN'S C$5.5B ALLIED GOLD BID IN JEOPARDY — BEIJING THE LONE HOLDOUT AS DEAL CLOCK TICKS
snippet: Zijin Gold International's friendly all-cash bid for Allied Gold Corporation (TSX: AAUC) at C$44/share — the largest acquisition in Zijin's history — has cleared Canadian regulatory approval and all international jurisdictions except one: Beijing. China's antitrust delay has put the C$5.5 billion deal at risk, with possible outcomes including a renegotiated lower price or a restructured transaction where Zijin takes a partial stake. Allied Gold's three African open-pit gold mines — Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, and Ethiopia — are the prize.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE +103% YOY AT 152,000 CNY/T — BATTERY STORAGE SUPPLANTS EVs AS THE DEMAND ENGINE
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate is trading at roughly 152,000 CNY/T — more than double year-ago levels — as a structural shift in demand moves lithium beyond its EV narrative. Utility-scale and industrial stationary storage demand jumped 71% in 2025 and analysts project another 55% gain in 2026, with data centre battery backup emerging as a surprise growth segment. Supply returning from Bald Hill and Finniss restarts has not dented the price rally, signalling the market believes end-demand growth outpaces new tonnes.

headline: CHILE COPPER OUTPUT FALLS 9.4% IN JULY — LME EX-U.S. STOCKS TIGHTEN AS COMEX PILES UP
snippet: Chile's copper output fell 9.4% year-on-year in July due to severe weather and mine maintenance, adding fundamental tightness to the non-U.S. copper market. LME inventories outside the United States are drawing down while Comex warehouses remain near record highs from tariff-driven front-loading — a bifurcated market that keeps prices near $6.50/lb despite rising macro headwinds including renewed U.S.-Iran tensions. Copper is still up 47% year-on-year; the pullback from the August 25 record high of $6.70/lb is being treated as consolidation.

headline: CANADIAN GOLDFIELDS WRAPS INAUGURAL DRILL AT SWAYZE CENTRAL — ONTARIO GOLD ASSAYS PENDING; TSXV: CGM
snippet: Canadian Goldfields Discovery Corp. (TSXV: CGM) has completed its inaugural six-hole, 1,422-metre diamond drill program at the Swayze Central Gold Project in Ontario, testing priority geochemical and geophysical targets. Assay results have not yet been returned and will be reported as they become available. The company also collected 1,808 B-horizon soil samples as part of an extensive geochemical survey running in parallel. Swayze is an emerging greenstone belt corridor in Northern Ontario with historical gold showings.

headline: WALLER PIVOT PRICED IN — BUT GOLD'S MUTED REACTION TELLS A DEEPER STORY ABOUT POSITIONING
snippet: When Fed Governor Waller effectively repriced half a rate hike out of the September FOMC, gold moved — but barely, which is the point. GoldSilver.com argues the muted reaction reveals how thoroughly the post-NFP selloff already priced in hawkish risk: gold is not cheap on bearish news, which is actually a bullish structural signal. The piece makes the case that institutional positioning remains underweight precious metals, and that the CPI print on September 12 is more likely to be a 'sell the rumour, buy the news' setup regardless of the outcome.

headline: CAN GOLD BREAK $5,000 IN SEPTEMBER? ANALYSTS SPLIT AS DECISIVE CPI WEEK BEGINS
snippet: With gold recovering to $4,465 after the NFP-driven selloff and rate-hike odds falling from 70% to 50%, analysts are debating whether a return to $5,000 is achievable in September. Bulls point to compressed positioning, structural central bank demand, and a seasonal tailwind; bears cite the still-elevated FOMC hike probability, a resilient U.S. dollar, and Goldman's freshly cut $4,900 year-end target as a ceiling. The August CPI print on September 12 — arriving just five days before the FOMC meets — is the fulcrum.
